lesson_title: A Bill Is a Claim, Not a Command: Creditors Reconciliation
hook_text: Their bill says R65 930. Your book says R48 660. Pay the wrong one and you lose R13 180.
clip_script: You run a spaza. Every week you fetch stock from the wholesaler and write in your exercise book what you took and what you paid. Month end, they send a bill: you owe us R65 930. Your book says R48 660. Do you simply pay their number? That is somebody else's book about your money. Do you refuse and stand on yours? Your book has holes too. So you sit down with both and go line by line — and the differences are only ever three kinds. Things that are late: an invoice still in the post, a payment they have not processed. Things you never knew about: interest for paying late, a discount for paying early, and nobody phoned you either time. And things that are simply wrong — because unlike a bank fee, the wholesaler's clerk is a person, and people put one customer's delivery on another customer's account. Fix what is yours: plus R7 200, minus R2 700, plus R540, minus R950. Fifty-two thousand seven hundred and fifty. That is what you honestly owe. The rest is theirs to fix. A supplier's bill is a claim, not a command.
visual_style: A spaza counter at dusk: a printed wholesaler statement on one side, a worn exercise book on the other, matching lines lighting up green and mismatches flaring amber until both totals settle on R52 750.
pacing: Punchy opening comparison, rhythmic line-by-line sort, firm closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and reconcile the statement yourself — line by line, before you pay a cent.
